name: Phuket
summary: Andaman beaches from Kata to Surin, Phuket Old Town's shophouses and food, Wat Chalong, and boat trips to Phang Nga Bay and Phi Phi's Maya Bay.

tips.title: Visa-free stays cut to 30 days
tips.body: From 15 September 2026 the 60-day visa exemption ended, and passport holders from 60 countries (including the UK, US and Australia) now get 30 days visa-free for tourism. Visa-free entries by land are generally limited to 2 per calendar year.

tips.title: Show funds and an onward ticket
tips.body: Visa-exempt visitors may be asked for at least 10,000 baht per person or 20,000 baht per family, plus proof of onward or return travel.

tips.title: Complete the TDAC within 3 days of arrival
tips.body: All foreign nationals have needed the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) since 1 May 2025. Submit it free in the 3 days before arrival at tdac.immigration.go.th.

tips.title: Obey red flags on the beach
tips.body: People have drowned in strong riptides, especially during the monsoon (roughly May to October on the Andaman coast). Follow beach flags and warning signs, and don't swim when red flags fly.

tips.title: Jellyfish risk May–October
tips.body: Jellyfish are more common from May to October, and some stings can be fatal. Get medical help quickly if you are stung.

tips.title: Jet-ski and motorbike rental scams
tips.body: Never give your passport as a deposit to jet-ski or motorbike rental businesses, which may hold it against made-up damage claims.

tips.title: Vapes are illegal, including for tourists
tips.body: Possessing or using any vape, e-cigarette, pod, e-liquid or heat-not-burn device is illegal, with no exceptions for tourists. Fines typically run 5,000–30,000 baht, plus confiscation and possible detention.

tips.title: Cannabis is medical-only
tips.body: Recreational cannabis is illegal again. Use requires a Thai-issued prescription limited to a 30-day supply, and taking cannabis out of the country without permission brings fines from 30,000 baht per kg.

tips.title: Scooters need an IDP and a helmet
tips.body: Carry a 1968 International Driving Permit (IDP) plus your home licence, and wear a helmet, which is required by law. Riding without the right licence can void your insurance.

tips.title: Insurance and emergency numbers
tips.body: Hospitals require a guarantee of payment, so travel insurance is essential. Call 191 for police, fire or ambulance, or 1669 for an ambulance.

tips.title: Use ATMs inside banks
tips.body: ATM skimming has been reported, so use machines inside bank branches and cover your PIN.

tips.title: Respect the monarchy and mind what you post
tips.body: Criticising the Thai monarchy carries long prison sentences. Posting photos online of people drinking or in clothing seen as inappropriate can also be illegal.
